position_in_era.historical_role: The Amador brothers (Raimundo and Rafael) coined the genre name 'blueslería' on this record — playing pure blues at the rhythm of bulerías. A primary precedent for the translation aesthetic at the heart of Dorantes' work: foreign vocabulary inhabits flamenco's body without dissolving it. The last record the Amador brothers made together, released also in the UK, US, and Japan.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 1987 on Nuevos Medios. Final album the Amador brothers recorded together; Raimundo subsequently left and Rafael continued solo.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Raimundo and Rafael Amador, brothers from Seville, formed Pata Negra after Veneno dissolved. Raimundo's flamenco guitar combined with Rafael's voice produced the 'blueslería' synthesis.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Andalusian Sevilla — Triana and the wider working-class flamenco circuit; later presented live in Paris and New York.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Flamenco guitar played as if blues; bulería palmas / compás carrying blues phrasing; band instrumentation drew on swing, reggae, jazz alongside cante.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Released also in England, the United States, and Japan — among the first nuevo-flamenco records to receive a substantial international release.
